newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks end higher as rebound continues.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks end higher as rebound continues.

text.p: Toronto stocks ended higher on Tuesday, extending Monday's rally as Canadian equities continued to rebound from last week's sharp losses.
The TSE 300 Composite Index gained 13.22 points to close at 5919.86 in brisk turnover of 98.6 million shares worth C$1.56 billion ($1.1 billion).
Advancing stocks outnumbered declines 489 to 473 with 314 issues unchanged.
"The market continued to recover from last week's Greenspan beating," said Rolie Bradley, an institutional salesman with Maison Placements Canada Inc.
The key 300 index sank about 3.4 percent last week following comments by U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan, which spooked financial markets worldwide.
The TSE recouped some of its losses on Monday with a 1.6 percent gain, buoyed by a rally in Canadian bonds. Bonds ended weaker on Tuesday due to profit taking.
Some stock analysts have said the upcoming season to invest in registered retirement savings plans should give the TSE momentum to move higher.
Statistics Canada said Tuesday Canadians will be able to contribute C$47 billion ($34 billion) to their RRSP plans in 1996, up three per cent from 1995.

But Bradley downplayed the impact of RRSPs on the market. "Everybody will tell you it's going to keep the market going, but it is not the major determining factor in the direction of the market," he said.
* Potash Corp. of Saskatchewan Inc. jumped 6.55 to 117.55 after the fertilizer giant acquired a 51 percent stake in Germany's Kali und Salz Beteiligungs AG.
* Agrium Inc. rose 0.35 to 19 on 2.3 million shares, the TSE's top issue by volume. Viridian Inc. shareholders approved a merger with Calgary-based Agrium on Tuesday.

* Bre-X Minerals Ltd. rose 0.60 to 20.65 on 1.5 million shares as investors awaited a final announcement on the company's talks with Barrick Gold Corp. over the Busang gold discovery. Barrick jumped 1.20 to close at 41.25.
